description: This pie chart details the distribution of mathematical topics within a dataset used for benchmarking large language models’ problem-solving skills. The chart contains twelve slices, each representing a different mathematical subject. “Algebra – High School” constitutes 17.83% (69) of the dataset, followed by “Combinatorics – Olympiad-level” at 9.56% (37). “Geometry – Olympiad-level” represents 6.46% (25), as does “Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra – University-level”. “Calculus and Analysis – University-level” accounts for 6.20% (24), while “Algebra – University-level” is 4.39% (17). “Probability – University-level” is 3.62% (14), matching “Differential Equations – University-level”. “Pre-Calculus – High School” represents 14.21% (55), and “Geometry – High School” is 3.62% (14). Finally, “Number Theory – Olympiad-level” is 1.03% (4). The chart includes a legend listing each topic and its corresponding color, as well as percentage and count labels displayed directly within each slice. The slices appear to be ordered visually in a clockwise direction, generally from largest to smallest proportion.
